A student walks at a constant speed for a distance of 50 m in a time of 40 s. The student rests for
a time of 10 s and then walks back to the starting point at a constant speed in a time of 30 s.
What is the distance–time graph for the motion of the student?

hints: Notice the y-axis is distance, not displacement - distance travelled keeps adding up even on the walk back to the start.
Split the $80\text{ s}$ total into three parts: walk out $0$ to $40\text{ s}$, rest $40\text{ s}$ to $50\text{ s}$, walk back $50\text{ s}$ to $80\text{ s}$.
Check what the distance value should be at $40\text{ s}$, $50\text{ s}$ and $80\text{ s}$: the return journey adds another $50\text{ m}$ to give $100\text{ m}$ total.
walkthrough: First stage: walk $50\text{ m}$ in $40\text{ s}$ at constant speed. On a distance-time graph this is a straight line from $(0,0)$ to $(40\text{ s}, 50\text{ m})$. Gradient is speed $= 50/40 = 1.25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Second stage: rest for $10\text{ s}$. Distance stays at $50\text{ m}$, so draw a horizontal line from $t = 40\text{ s}$ to $t = 50\text{ s}$.

Third stage: walk back $50\text{ m}$ in $30\text{ s}$. Distance does not go back to zero, it increases by another $50\text{ m}$ from $50\text{ m}$ to $100\text{ m}$ between $t = 50\text{ s}$ and $t = 80\text{ s}$.
This return line is steeper than the first line because the same $50\text{ m}$ is covered in a shorter time, speed $= 50/30 \approx 1.67\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Only the graph with rise to $50\text{ m}$ at $40\text{ s}$, flat to $50\text{ s}$, then rise to $100\text{ m}$ at $80\text{ s}$ matches. This is option D

A.explanation: Shows distance falling back to $0\text{ m}$ at $80\text{ s}$. Distance travelled cannot decrease, and it reaches $50\text{ m}$ too early.

B.explanation: Shows distance continuing to increase, but reaches $50\text{ m}$ at about $30\text{ s}$ instead of $40\text{ s}$.

C.explanation: Shows the correct timings but distance falls to $0\text{ m}$. This is the displacement-time graph, not the distance-time graph.

D.explanation: Shows $0$ to $50\text{ m}$ in $40\text{ s}$, flat from $40\text{ s}$ to $50\text{ s}$, then $50\text{ m}$ to $100\text{ m}$ in $30\text{ s}$ as distance keeps accumulating.
